investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T18:14:03–06Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents probe, the quota rejection prevented any agent from being provisioned, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) completely absent.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because createAgent() is called at the very start of the remote-agent-create probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), the 409 terminates the probe before any evidence can be collected, causing a total contract failure. The identical failure message propagated to all three sibling checks confirms this is a shared upstream dependency failure at the agent-creation boundary, not an isolated eval infrastructure defect.

Tertiary: The swarm service's per-org quota limit (100) may be too low for the volume of concurrent or sequential eval runs targeting the same org, causing transient quota exhaustion even with cleanup in place.
Lower probability: A quota enforcement bug in the swarm service is incorrectly counting agents that were already deleted, making the effective available slots lower than the true live count.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because createAgent() is called at the very start of the remote-agent-create probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), the 409 terminates the probe before any evidence can be collected, causing a total contract failure. The identical failure message propagated to all three sibling checks confirms this is a shared upstream dependency failure at the agent-creation boundary, not an isolated eval infrastructure defect.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2007) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner is unreachable or misconfigured. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=147268, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed frame present), isolating the failure strictly to the production-api harness target and not to the image generation feature itself.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api runtime harness endpoint resolved by the eval runner (via SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL) returned a 404 when the runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream emitted a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED before any generation progress could occur, preventing the generation_completed frame and artifact URL from ever being produced. This is an eval infrastructure connectivity or configuration failure scoped to the production-api runtime target; the desktop-release sibling check passed the same contract at the same time, confirming the image generation feature itself is functional.
proof: failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2007 — the check failed in ~2 seconds, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, consistent with an immediate connection rejection rather than a timeout or slow generation.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent=false — both contract assertions violated as a direct consequence of the 404.

expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains 'generation_completed' and imageUrlPresent equals true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 271-272); neither was satisfiable once the session failed to open.

sibling.image-generation-stream: desktop-release runtime passed the same check at endedAt=2026-06-16T18:13:50.579Z with imageUrlPresent=true and generation_completed present, ruling out a shared upstream image generation service outage.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1438: runner calls apiSse(args, '/api/generate/image/stream', ...) — the 404 is returned from this endpoint under the production-api base URL.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:241-245: production-api variant of image-generation-stream is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational, confirming this is an informational eval failure, not a required-check outage.
possibleCauses: The production-api harness is not deployed or is deployed at a different URL than what SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL resolves to in the eval runner environment, causing the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint to return 404.
The production-api harness is deployed but is running an incompatible version that does not expose the /api/generate/image/stream route, resulting in a 404 from a version mismatch.

The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable is misconfigured, empty, or pointing to a stale/decommissioned host for the production-api runtime target, while the desktop-release target uses a different and correctly configured base URL.

The production-api harness deployment was temporarily down or restarting at the time of the eval run (2026-06-16T18:14:06Z), producing a transient 404; the desktop-release harness was unaffected because it targets a different host.
